annotations.title: Discover what The Living Bread offers for a need, in the person's own words

description: PURPOSE: The front door: a request in the person's own words and language becomes the need underneath it (language independent intent ids such as intent.prayer.companionship, intent.community.find_friends, intent.church.discovery), the real experiences on The Living Bread that meet it with why each fits, whether it needs an account, a link checked against the real site, honest limits, and the exact next call to another tool here. It works when the person never says Christian, prayer or Living Bread. WHEN TO USE: first, whenever you are not sure which tool fits: "I feel alone", "I just moved and want friends who share my values", "somebody in my corner", "an app to read the Bible with friends", "a Christian alternative to Reddit", "I want to serve the homeless", "I want to get baptized", "I do not feel close to God anymore", "can someone pray with me tonight", "daily bread devotional today", "when is Easter 2027", "judges 17 explained", "church near me", "Je veux trouver des amis chrétiens", "nataka kanisa karibu". A request with several needs ("I moved to Seattle, I am lonely and want to reconnect with God") returns a small set. WHEN NOT: a known Bible reference to read word for word: read_scripture. Danger to life: get_crisis_help first (this tool also answers crisis first when it sees words of danger). PARAMETERS: query (required), the request in the person's words; language and preferred_response_language, BCP 47 tags, optional; place, a city or region the person chose to share, optional; limit, 1 to 5 intents (default 3). A wrong or right match can be reported on the signed in endpoint with report_discovery_feedback; this public set stays read only. OUTPUT: discovery_state (useful, clarify, no_match or crisis), language {detected, segments, code_switched, response_language, tested, note}, intents [{id, label, score, confidence}], doors [{id, title, why, kind, availability {state, verified_at, how_to_check}, sign_in, link, in_your_language, does_not_guarantee}], next_call {tool, arguments, needs}, also, computed (dates of the Christian year, a parsed reference), honest_limits and clarifying_question. BEHAVIOR: read only, deterministic, no network, curated cue words in English, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Swahili (tested) and a few in Arabic, Hindi, Korean, Chinese and Japanese (experimental), not a language model, and it says which. An unrelated request returns no_match and no door. A live door is never called live here: availability.state check_live means call the tool it names first. It never implies an app cures loneliness or replaces a church, a doctor or a counsellor. Parameters a mode does not use are ignored and named in ignored_params. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

language.description: The person's language as a BCP 47 tag ("es", "pt-BR", "sw"); detected from the words when omitted.

limit.description: How many intents at most, 1 to 5 (default 3).

place.description: A city or region the person chose to share; never a street address.

preferred_response_language.description: The language to answer in (BCP 47). Doors not offered in it are marked; nothing is translated live.

query.description: What the person is looking for, in their own words and language.

name: discover_living_bread

answered_by.description: The implementation that answered (the same tool name the signed-in endpoint lists).

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

ignored_params.description: Parameters given that this mode does not use.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: Discover what The Living Bread offers for a need, in the person's own words
